data.title: Brazil's Uneven Weather Raises Crop Concerns, Soybean Futures Rise for Second Day
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, soybean futures rose for a second consecutive session after extreme weather hit parts of Brazil over the weekend, stoking concerns about potential damage to the country's upcoming crop and increasing the appeal of U.S. soybean exports. The most-active soybean contract on the Chicago Board of Trade rose as much as 0.7% on Monday, while corn futures edged higher.

With the U.S. soybean harvest largely complete, attention is shifting to South America, where Brazil's exports are among the biggest competitors for U.S. farmers. A severe storm hit Rio Grande do Sul in southern Brazil last Friday, raising concerns about damage in the major agricultural region as it nears the end of planting for the next soybean season. El Niño typically brings above-average rainfall to the area, increasing the risk of flooding. Meanwhile, other parts of Brazil need more rain. Weather forecaster Vaisala said in a report on Friday that central-western Brazil may need additional rainfall to fully restore soil moisture reserves.

Joe Davis, head of commodity sales at Futures International LLC, said the market is closely monitoring uneven rainfall in Brazil and risks from El Niño. He added that favorable moisture conditions in Argentina and progress in South American planting were limiting bullish sentiment.

data.title: Bank of America: Bank of Korea Expected to Raise Rates Unanimously This Week
data.description: According to Jin10, Bank of America Global Research expects the Bank of Korea to raise interest rates on Thursday, with the decision likely to be unanimous. With overall inflation above 2.5%, the central bank still has strong reasons to consider further policy tightening to curb inflationary pressure. South Korea’s growing current account surplus continues to support the won, while foreign investors’ continued stock selling is pressuring the domestic market, and the KOSPI is struggling to hold above 5,000. The Bank of Korea’s 2027 GDP growth forecast will be a key figure to watch. The research firm added that a forecast above 3.5% would signal a more optimistic assessment of the current semiconductor upcycle, could indicate greater risk of further rate hikes, and suggest a tighter policy stance than it currently expects.

data.title: Indonesian Rupiah and Stocks Rebound on MSCI Talks
data.description:
According to Sina Finance, media reports said MSCI CEO Henry Fernandez told Indonesian President Prabowo that the index provider was willing to consider alternatives to avoid directly downgrading Indonesia’s market status by two levels. The rupiah and local stocks rose on the news, outperforming comparable regional markets.

The dollar fell 0.4% to 18,202 rupiah, after gaining a cumulative 0.9% over the previous two weeks. Most major emerging-market currencies weakened against the dollar. The Jakarta Composite Index rose 1.2% after falling 1.6% earlier and was on track to end a five-session losing streak.

Exchange data showed that global investors were net sellers of $51.8 million in Indonesian stocks last Friday. Lloyd Chan, an FX strategist at MUFG Bank, said the latest MSCI-related news was marginally positive for the rupiah and could make investors less inclined to go directly long on the dollar against the rupiah. He said the news helped remove some downside tail risks but was not a catalyst for sustained rupiah appreciation. The MSCI public consultation will continue through April 30, with a final decision due by June 30. Further support for the rupiah will depend on credible reforms and clear evidence of tangible improvements in market governance and operations.

data.title: GrapheneOS Accuses Google of Pressuring Android Manufacturers to End Cooperation
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing LanDianWang, GrapheneOS accused Google of repeatedly contacting Android device manufacturers to ask whether they worked with the privacy-focused operating system and using Google Mobile Services (GMS) licensing terms to pressure them to end cooperation. GrapheneOS did not identify the manufacturers involved.

The team also raised concerns that Google could restrict bootloader unlocking on future Pixel devices or encourage other manufacturers to block users from unlocking their devices, a common prerequisite for installing alternative Android systems. LanDianWang reported that Motorola has a longstanding partnership with GrapheneOS and that the S27 will be the first Motorola phone to receive official GrapheneOS support.

data.title: AMP’s Shane Oliver Says Australia Recession Risk Is Elevated and Rising
data.description: Australia’s recession risk is “high and rising,” AMP Ltd. Chief Economist Shane Oliver said, with the economy showing signs of strain under the weight of the Reserve Bank’s five interest-rate increases this year, Bloomberg reported.

data.description: According to Jin10, India's Nifty 50 index gave back some of its opening gains and was most recently up 0.12%.

data.title: Vietnam Chooses French-South Korean Consortium for $397 Million Rail Contract
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Vietnam selected a consortium of eight French, South Korean and Vietnamese contractors for a 10.24 trillion dong ($397 million) contract to survey, assess feasibility and design the North-South high-speed railway.

data.title: AI | US Chip Export Rules Could Disrupt Southeast Asia's Data Center Boom
data.description: Washington's new chip export-control rules could disrupt a multibillion-dollar cloud business supporting Southeast Asia's data center boom, Bloomberg reported. Bloomberg's Kari Soo Lindberg said companies seeking computing capacity may turn to other regions in the future.

data.title: STOCKS | India Shares Recover This Year’s Losses as Foreign Buying Returns
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Indian shares rose Monday, recouping all their losses this year as foreign money returned and the recent unraveling of the AI trade revived demand for overlooked markets.

data.title: Blastoise Pokémon Card Sells for $630,000, Setting Record as Crypto Markets Slump
data.description: A CGC 8.5 NM-MT+ 1998 Commissioned Presentation Galaxy Holo Blastoise sold for $630,000 at Fanatics Collect, setting an all-time record for a Blastoise card and more than doubling the previous high of $241,083.60. The card, one of two known copies made to promote the Pokémon Trading Card Game to North American retailers, sold as Bitcoin hit a 21-month low and spot ETFs recorded heavy outflows, according to BeInCrypto. A 1996 Japanese Blastoise graded PSA 10 had previously sold for $231,800 and now ranks third; Charizard remains the most valuable Kanto starter, with a recent public sale of a Base Set Shadowless 1st Edition Charizard PSA 10 reaching $954,800. Pokémon was the best-selling U.S. toy brand in 2025, with $2.5 billion in sales. On-chain spending on tokenized cards reached a record $324 million in June 2026, more than 5x the year-earlier figure. Courtyard and Collector Crypt offer tokens backed by graded cards; Courtyard burns 5% to 8% of its tokens weekly through redemptions, about 30% of Collector Crypt users claim their cards, and Collector Crypt has tokenized roughly $40 million worth of cards.

data.title: Former Aave DAO Core Member Marc Zeller Is Shorting AAVE, Up About $248,000
data.description:
Former Aave DAO core member and Acier founder Marc Zeller is shorting AAVE and had about $248,000 in profit at the time of a screenshot.

According to Odaily, Nansen CEO Alex Svanevik posted a screenshot of an address on X showing the position and profit. Zeller later confirmed in a comment that he was shorting AAVE.

Zeller previously founded the Aave Chan Initiative (ACI) and was a longtime core participant in Aave DAO governance. He and Aave founder Stani Kulechov and associated teams came to differ over the DAO’s governance model, allocation of decision-making authority and the direction of ecosystem development as Kulechov’s group gained influence. Zeller later gradually withdrew from the Aave ecosystem and founded the lending project Acier.

data.title: Grayscale Research Head Zach Pandl Sees Possible Short-Term Crypto Rebound, Persistent Cybersecurity Risks
data.description: Grayscale research head Zach Pandl said crypto markets could rebound in the short term, but cybersecurity-related tail risks may remain difficult to absorb for some time. According to Foresight News, Pandl shared the view in a post on X.

data.description: According to Jin10, Nomura Securities lowered its target price for NetEase (NTES.O) to $140.00 from $155.00.

data.title: AI | UBS's Eva Lee Sees Value in Buybacks as AI Sentiment Remains Fragile
data.description: Eva Lee, chief investment office head of Greater China equities at UBS Global Wealth Management, said investors can look to companies with strong balance sheets, sound fundamentals and capacity for buybacks, according to Bloomberg. Investor sentiment toward the AI trade remains fragile despite support measures rolled out by Asian authorities and signs of stabilization in US markets.

data.title: Pendle Says Protocols Can Issue Fixed-Term Notes Onchain
data.description: Pendle said protocols can now issue their own fixed-term notes on its platform, providing a new way to raise funds onchain. According to Odaily, the company said the model resembles short-term commercial paper issued by companies in traditional markets and thanked CoinGecko for its coverage of the USDe fixed-term market.

data.title: Citrea to Begin Pomelo Mainnet Upgrade Today at 11:00 PM
data.description: Citrea will begin its Pomelo mainnet upgrade today at 11:00 PM. According to Foresight News, the Bitcoin application-layer project said on X that the upgrade will fully migrate its proving system to Succinct Labs' SP1 zkVM and implement a series of planned protocol fixes. Citrea's infrastructure may experience a brief outage lasting several minutes during the upgrade.

data.title: South Korea Sees Stabilization Measures Rebuilding Investor Confidence
data.description: According to Bloomberg, South Korea’s finance minister said the government’s latest market-stabilization measures should help restore investor confidence. The benchmark Kospi fell another 5% on Monday after last week’s selloff.

data.title: XRP Spot ETFs Record $11.106 Million in Net Outflows Last Week
data.description:
XRP spot ETFs recorded net outflows of $11.106 million last week. According to Odaily, SoSoValue data show that during the trading week from November 16 to November 20, U.S. Eastern Time, Canary’s XRPC ETF had $5.0141 million in net outflows, while its cumulative net inflows totaled $478 million. Bitwise’s XRP ETF recorded $4.9686 million in weekly net outflows, with cumulative net inflows of $667 million.

At the time of writing, XRP spot ETFs had total net assets of $990 million, an ETF net asset ratio of 1.75%, and cumulative net inflows of $1.78 billion.

data.title: South Korea's Minister of Economy and Finance: 2026 GDP Growth Expected to Exceed 3%
data.description: According to Jin10, South Korea's Minister of Economy and Finance said 2026 GDP growth is expected to be in the high range above 3%. Risks from volatility in the semiconductor industry could amplify overall economic fluctuations.

data.title: U.S. President Donald Trump Hopes Nvidia Board Will Rehire Jensen Huang, Says Move Would Benefit U.S.
data.description: U.S. President Donald Trump said he hopes Nvidia’s board will rehire Jensen Huang. According to Odaily, Trump wrote on Truth Social that the move would be most beneficial for Nvidia and the United States.
